analysis.title: Global Data Centers: New constraints (inflation, financing), but capacity growth still compelling
key_insights: MS forecasts global data center IT capacity growing +180 GW (+23% pa) from 2026e to 2030e, from about 136 GW at end-2026e to about 316 GW in 2030e.
The US adds the most capacity 2026e-30e (+88 GW), then China (+49 GW), Europe (+12 GW), India (+7 GW), SE Asia (+6 GW) and the Middle East (+3 GW).
Year-end 2026e capacity: US 65 GW, China 32 GW, Europe 10 GW. 2026e growth: US +31%, China +22%, Europe +18%.
First bull and bear cases: bull reaches 377 GW by 2030 (+28% pa) if energy, planning, supply lines and construction timing ease. Bear reaches 240 GW (+17% pa) with restrictions across all Five Ps.
AlphaWise survey (July, US, China, UK, France, Spain): energy is the top bottleneck. Speed of access to electricity is cited by 27% of operators overall and 45% in the US.

New constraints are emerging: financing, memory (China's top bottleneck at 29%), powered land, and chips/GPUs. Over the next two years operators expect funding (14%) and water access (17%) to matter more.

Build costs are the next big debate. Operators report +12% cost inflation over the past 12 months and expect +15% pa over the next two years (US +17%, China +18%). Cost per GW has risen from $30bn in 2022/23 toward $50-60bn by the end of the decade.
At +8% average inflation to 2030, total build cost rises about 50% in five years. The note asks whether builders scale back capacity or absorb higher capex.
MS projects a US power shortfall of 70 GW for 2026-28 before 'time to power' solutions. After those solutions it is 43 GW, and 38 GW including APAC spillover.

US developers may host capacity abroad. Candidates are Europe, South Korea, Japan, India, SE Asia, Australia and the Middle East. The key factors are passive build cost and energy cost. MS sees about +20 GW of excess non-China capacity in the base case and +27 GW in the bull case.
AI-related credit issuance is $471bn YTD through mid-October 2026, about 2.2x the $216bn issued in FY25. Credit markets are becoming more selective.

HQ hyperscalers (AMZN, MSFT, GOOGL, META) are over 75% of 2027E cash capex. They have ample debt capacity. Lower-rated hyperscalers and neoclouds face higher funding costs and may need secured or credit-supported financing.
CRWV unsecured debt trades above 1,000bp, within 60bp of the CCC index. The CDS AI basket trades more than 60bp wider than CDX IG. HQ hyperscalers trade about 5bp wider than the IG index.
Data center ABS supply is slowing as rates rise, and new-issue ABS yields have spiked. Modeled project returns are more sensitive to lease economics than to debt coupon and coverage assumptions.

Planning pushback is rising in the US: an estimated $156bn of projects were cancelled or delayed in 2025 and $130bn in 1Q26 alone. A Gallup poll finds 70% of Americans oppose local data centers. MS tracks more than 250 delayed projects.

State actions include a Pennsylvania executive order ending fast-track permitting, a New York 50+ MW permit pause, a Texas ERCOT audit, and the abandoned $25bn Digital Gateway project in Northern Virginia.

Europe has long-standing constraints. Ireland's moratorium ended in December 2025 with conditions, including 80% additional renewable supply. Spain proposes hourly renewable matching. Denmark deprioritised data centers in its grid queue. Scotland paused planning decisions for projects over 50 MW.
Memory prices are up more than 6x in 12 months, which MS calls a structural reset driven by AI demand for HBM and DRAM.
Powered land inflation is above 40% over five years in the US and above 70% in Europe. Secondary US markets are 50-90% cheaper than Northern Virginia.

China forecast: 26 GW in 2025 to 80 GW by 2030e, with Rmb8.5tr of capex. Domestic GPU shipments rise from 1.1mn units in 2025 to 2.4mn in 2026e and 4.8mn in 2027e. HBM is the biggest bottleneck. China powershell cost is $3mn per MW against $16mn per MW in the US.
Europe forecast: +21% pa to 2030, 41 GW by 2035 in the base case, 84 GW bull, 22 GW bear. Sovereign data centers are expected to be under 10% of new build.

India capacity is expected to rise from 1.8 GW in FY26e to 10.5 GW in FY31e, about $70bn of investment. South Korea is expected to add about 2 GW, with about 5 GW announced by five operators. Australia is expected to rise from 1.8 GW to 6.1 GW by 2030 (+31% CAGR).
Electrical equipment suppliers reported DC order growth in the 'triple digits'. Q2 2026 gas turbine orders hit a record 38GW. MS thinks 2026 is the peak for gas turbine orders.

European macro: data center capex of about EUR34bn in 2026 and EUR56bn in 2027 is worth 0.2pp and 0.3pp of euro area GDP, but the actual GDP impact is under half that because of imports (over 50 cents of every euro goes to NVIDIA GPUs).

earnings_insights: Schneider, ABB and Siemens cited data center order growth in the 'triple digits' in 1H26 results, and Legrand cited about 30%.
Legrand updated its FY27-30 data center organic revenue CAGR to mid to high teens.
MS sees 6% upside to consensus 2027 EBIT at Legrand, and 5.4% (Schneider) and 5.1% (Legrand) above VA consensus 2027 EBIT. These are MS estimates against consensus, not reported figures.
Siemens Energy FY26 results and new 2030 targets are due on 11 November. Data centers are about 28% of Gas Services customer commitments and 42% of group orders.

Vertiv organic revenue growth has been above 40% in the Americas over the last 12 months, while EMEA has been declining since 3Q25. Vertiv said the 'European spring is uncoiling' and expects growth to return in 2H.
Merlin's 1H26 results: 160MW let or pre-let, with 180MW in Lisbon in advanced negotiations. Neoclouds are about 85% of data center rent, and CoreWeave is 9% of total rents.

risk_factors: Power access: speed of access to electricity is the top bottleneck, especially in the US (45%), and a 38-70 GW US shortfall through 2028.
Build cost inflation compounding at +12-15% pa, with memory up more than 6x.
Financing: credit markets are becoming more selective, lower-rated issuers (neoclouds) face wider spreads, and ABS issuance is slowing as rates rise.
Planning and community opposition: US state and local moratoria, an estimated $156bn of projects delayed or cancelled in 2025, and 70% of Americans opposed to local data centers.
Regulatory tightening in Europe: the Spanish draft Royal Decree, Irish conditions, and the Scottish and Danish pauses.
Labour shortages and water access, with water expected to become a larger bottleneck by 2028.
Possible pre- or double-ordering of electrical equipment, and a gas turbine order peak in 2026.
Potential oversupply in Korea from capacity concentrated in 2029-30.
Middle East security risk after recent regional conflict.
Hyperscaler capex sustainability and returns on AI investment falling short of expectations.

Exhibit 8/43: Global credit issuance for AI is $471bn YTD-26 against $132bn YTD-25 and $216bn FY25. HQ hyperscaler USD issuance is $132bn YTD-26.
Exhibit 46: CRWV unsecured weighted-average OAS trades above 1,000bp, within 60bp of the CCC index.
Exhibit 133: 2Q26 quarterly gas turbine orders of 38GW are the highest quarter in history and above the year-2000 peaks.
Exhibit 136: The EU cap goods data center valuation discount to the US is -18% on 1-year forward EV/EBIT, against a peak discount of -27% in May-26.
vol_and_positioning: The CDS AI basket trades more than 60bp wider than CDX IG.
HQ hyperscalers trade about 5bp wider than the IG index, after leading the June-July spread widening.
CRWV unsecured debt trades at an average above 1,000bp OAS, within 60bp of the CCC index.

Natural gas pipeline stocks have underperformed in recent months on data center pushback, a WSJ article on onsite power costs, and higher long-dated Treasury yields. MS sees entry points in the pullback.
geopolitical: US federal permitting acceleration for data centers (July 2025 executive order) against growing state and local moratoria.
Recent regional military conflict in the Middle East raised security concerns for data centers there, and DCs were targeted.
US export restrictions on Nvidia GPUs to China, with a presumption of denial on Hopper and Blackwell. A possible approval of the RTX 5500Pro was reported.
European data sovereignty push (Draghi report, EU-US Data Privacy Framework, US CLOUD Act conflict with GDPR).
Tariffs on electronic equipment raise US data center capital goods costs.
Ireland, Spain, Greece, Denmark and Scotland are tightening grid and renewable requirements for data centers.

tension_points.theme: data center capacity growth versus constraints
tension_points.bull_case: Compute demand exceeds supply for years. MS projects 316 GW by 2030e (+23% pa), operators are 99% confident of meeting 2030 build targets, and 52% of US operators expect spending to peak in 2028.
tension_points.bear_case: Power, planning, price, people and priority constraints, rising rates and local moratoria could limit capacity to 240 GW (+17% pa), with $130bn of projects delayed in 1Q26 alone.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Evidence of restrictions across all Five Ps, such as continued US state moratoria, build cost inflation near +15% pa, or credit markets closing to lower-rated issuers, would push toward the 240 GW bear case.

tension_points.bull_case: HQ hyperscalers (AMZN, MSFT, GOOGL, META) are rated about AA, hold over 75% of 2027E cash capex, and can absorb higher funding costs. Capital is still available and MS sees line of sight to 25%+ ROIC for top players.
tension_points.bear_case: Credit is becoming more selective, ABS supply is slowing, and neoclouds such as CRWV trade near CCC spreads and may need contractual credit support or a slower build timetable.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A further widening in the CDS AI basket beyond the current 60bp-plus gap to CDX IG, or failed financings by lower-rated issuers.

tension_points.bull_case: CoreWeave and Nebius capture higher pricing from supply constraints, and CoreWeave cites better contribution margins on recent contracts.
tension_points.bear_case: Execution risk in scaling active power on tight timelines, capital intensity, and uncertainty about raising capital at attractive rates.

tension_points.theme: gas pipeline stocks and data centers
tension_points.bull_case: New onsite power and pipeline project announcements should drive outperformance into year-end, and WMB is materially mispriced against data center growth.
tension_points.bear_case: State-level data center pushback, limited recent project announcements, concerns about hyperscaler capex and debt issuance, and higher long-dated Treasury yields.
tension_points.what_invalidates: No new onsite power or pipeline project announcements over the next few months, or further state regulatory hurdles in Texas, Pennsylvania and Ohio.

tension_points.bull_case: Triple-digit data center order growth, a favourable price/cost set-up in 2027 and 2027 EBIT 5-6% above consensus.
tension_points.bear_case: Orders may reflect pre- or double-ordering, and gas turbine orders may peak in 2026 with moderation in 2027.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A sharp normalization of order intake, or a moderation in gas turbine orders larger than expected in 2027.
